title: Alpha4 principle multi-dataset validation
research_question: Do Alpha4's frozen local-design principles transfer beyond ECG200 and GunPoint across several additional small univariate time-series classification datasets?
hypothesis: The frozen Alpha4 principle—contiguous 16-sample local Fourier/KAN blocks with local output width 16 and k=[1,2], followed by one Fourier/KAN classification head—will achieve >=0.80 mean Q.ANT TEST accuracy on at least two of three preregistered transfer datasets while maintaining <=1.0 mean reference/Q.ANT prediction disagreements per TEST set.
scientific_boundary: This is a preregistered transfer benchmark, not architecture search. No dataset-specific topology, frequency, optimizer, epoch, or TEST-driven tuning is permitted.
frozen_model_rule: For adapted length L divisible by 16: L/16 contiguous windows; each Q.ANT Fourier/KAN 16→16; concatenate L features; Q.ANT Fourier/KAN L→n_classes; k=[1,2]. Only mechanically required input/head dimensions vary.

data_protocol.test_usage: No selection or tuning from TEST.

training_protocol.preprocessing: raw archive values after preregistered deterministic center crop

success_criteria: Supported if at least 2 of 3 datasets have mean Q.ANT TEST accuracy >=0.80 and every dataset has mean reference/Q.ANT prediction disagreements <=1.0 per TEST set.
promotion_rule: No architecture promotion. Success motivates a broader benchmark; failure localizes where the Alpha4 principle stops transferring.
hardware_boundary: Q.ANT CPU/software simulation only; no physical photonic hardware performance claim.
